## Delivered — the dispatch map's field-safety overlay, and the twenty-third door, 1 October 2026 (web; the door is contract only)

An operator choosing which nurse to send to Soweto while a panic was open in Soweto was reading two screens and
reconciling them by hand. The overlay groups the desk queue's own rows by suburb and draws them under the map the
controller already dispatches against, so the two pictures of one afternoon are one arithmetic. Nothing was
connected to anything: the counts are ours, from `GET /v1/safety/desk-queue@1`'s rows, and no new route, no store
and no figure that outlives the render that drew it. The door — feed #23, `crime-statistics` — landed in the
commit before this one (`f0bc96c7`) and is recorded here because it is what the overlay was written beside, and
because the two are easily mistaken for one feature: **the overlay draws no crime data and never will.** It draws
our own open panics and overdues. Feed #23 is a seam, connected to nothing.

| What landed | What it refuses, and what did not move | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **A list of suburbs with what is open in each**, under the dispatch map: the suburb, its counts, the two kinds, and a proportion of its nurses. Drawn from the live desk queue on every render, grouped by suburb and sorted by name | **No score, no rate over time, no trend and no ranking of suburbs** (`no-zone-risk-score`). A ranking of suburbs needs a record of what happened in each, and `geography.json#privacy`'s `no-history-drawn` is arranged against keeping one. There is also no reviewer here qualified for the call a score would make — whether a patient is seen at home or on a screen. A row carries five counts (`zone`, `panics`, `overdues`, `open`, `rostered`) and none of the five fields `neverCarries` names: `nurse`, `position`, `service`, `score`, `history`. Held by substring, so a field cannot slip in under another name. Sorted by name, proven by a fixture of three suburbs whose three orderings all disagree | `packages/engines/src/safety/domain/zone-overlay.ts` (+ its own test), `apps/web/src/lib/field-safety.ts`, `features/Dispatch.tsx`, `surface/office-identity.css` |
| **A denominator floor.** `zone-share-minimum-nurses` (proposed 5, bounds 3–20, unit `nurses`) suppresses the *proportion* below it, with the contract's own sentence saying how many nurses there are and why that is too few | **THE COUNT IS DRAWN WHATEVER THE FLOOR IS.** An open panic in a suburb with one nurse on the roster is exactly the incident the operator most needs to see, and a suppression rule that hid it would be a safety feature protecting a suburb's reputation instead of a person. The floor governs the proportion alone. It waits on **no** clinical review and that is asserted, not assumed: nothing about it is clinical and it decides nothing about a patient — it is k-anonymity over a roster count. Its bounds are what make it so: no value below three can be set, and its guardrail forbids `[0, 2, 21]`, the 2 being one below the lowest bound so the guardrail proves the floor rather than asserting it | `packages/catalog/field-safety.json` (defaults version 6), `packages/engines/src/safety/domain/settings.ts` + its test, `apps/web/src/lib/settings.ts`, `docs/governance/CLINICAL-REVIEW-PACK.md` |
| **Drawn for the operator alone, by a gate derived from the contract.** `maySeeFieldSafety()` reads the desk queue route's own `callers` and asks the vetting register which role the audience's subject holds | No audience string is typed at the gate, and the default is *not drawn* rather than drawn: a board that gained an audience later would gain the overlay silently, and the failure that produces is the back office reading a nurse's panic on a funding screen. The back office's `Operations` tab passes its audience down and gets no overlay, because its subject is an admin and the route admits an operator — it refuses for the reason the contract gives. If the route's callers ever widen, the overlay widens in the same edit | `apps/web/src/features/Dispatch.tsx`, `features/Admin.tsx`, `features/portal/Operations.tsx`, `shells/StaffShell.tsx`, `AdminShell.tsx`, `lib/roster.ts` (`rosteredIn`) |
| **Colour marks an incident, never a place.** An open panic tints that row's counts, beside a sentence that already says "1 panic" | **No colour on this overlay is a grade** (`a-zone-is-not-a-verdict`). No sentence names a suburb as safe or unsafe, and no zone circle is shaded: "Soweto is high risk" is a claim about a place made by a count of three; "two nurses are past check-out in Soweto" is a thing an operator can act on in the next minute. The build refuses a `.zone-shade`, a background on a row, or the overlay's figures reaching `LiveMap` | `apps/web/src/surface/office-identity.css`, `scripts/check-boundaries.mjs` |
| **Feed #23, the SAPS seam, linked through Safety** (commit `f0bc96c7`) | A door and not a connection: `crime-statistics` declares what the statistics for an area say and **what they may never be made to decide**. Connected to no supplier, no endpoint and no emitter, and `apis/safety.json` names it as a door. The overlay above draws no crime data and no suburb verdict, which is the difference between a seam and a decision | `packages/catalog/feeds.json`, `apis/safety.json` |

**Why a list and not a colour on the zones.** The roster has six suburbs and `geography.json` draws five circles,
so Tembisa and Alexandra are on the roster and drawn nowhere. A colouring would drop an open incident in either;
a list cannot. The contract's `_listNotAColourNote` justifies itself by those suburbs' names, and the build asks
it to name every suburb the roster holds and geography draws no circle for — prose naming suburbs is what goes
stale quietly when a roster changes, leaving a contract justifying a decision with examples that no longer exist.

**The patient's first view.** Unchanged, and it must stay so: the overlay is drawn from `features/Dispatch.tsx`,
which sits in the staff chunk behind a dynamic import, and touches neither `LiveMap` nor `geography.json`.

**Verified on the finished tree.** `npm run check` green, and `scripts/check-boundaries.mjs` green with its new
block printing its own line: *a list over 6 rostered suburbs, 2 of which (Tembisa, Alexandra) the map draws no
circle for; a row carries 5 counts and none of the 5 fields it never carries, by name and not by count; the floor
of 5 nurses governs the proportion alone, so 1 open panic in a suburb of 1 nurse is drawn whole while its
proportion is refused; the domain keeps nothing between draws; and the audience is read from
`GET /v1/safety/desk-queue@1`'s 1 caller rather than typed.* The eleven node suites pass — engines **513 of 513**,
including the eight overlay tests, among them `THE COUNT IS DRAWN WHATEVER THE FLOOR IS`. Every one of the twenty
new checks was **proven to fire by breaking its source and watching the build fail**, then restoring: a ranking
sort, a `nurse` field, a `score` field, a floored count, a proportion below the floor, a module cache, a mutable
binding, the grouping moved to module scope, a typed audience, an underived gate, a missing panic marker, a shaded
zone, a row background, the overlay fed to `LiveMap`, a note that drops Tembisa, a bound lowered to 2, a guardrail
that stops naming 2, a unit of minutes, a type that is not `count`, and a `drawnFor` naming no such route. The
restore was checked byte-faithful against a backup, and `npm run generate`'s field-safety, sentinel and
review-pack emitters were re-run and produced **no blob change**, so nothing drifted.

**Not verified, and why.** **The Playwright journeys did not run, including the new `tests/zone-field-safety.spec.ts`
(5 tests × 2 viewports).** Chromium cannot launch in this environment: `browserType.launch` fails with
`signal 11 SEGV_ACCERR`, and `os.cpus()` returns empty so Playwright also misdetects this arm64 machine as
`mac-x64` and looks for a browser build that does not exist. Both are sandbox limits, not code failures — the same
tree's node suites, typecheck and boundary checks all pass, and the spec was written and read rather than run. It is
**unverified by execution** and must be run on a machine where a browser launches before this is called done. The
iOS and Android builds were not run either. **Since verified (1 October 2026):** the release audit at HEAD
`a37cd638` ran `tests/zone-field-safety.spec.ts` and it passed 10 of 10 (5 tests × 2 viewports), and both native
builds — `xcodebuild` for the simulator and `:app:assembleDebug :app:lintDebug` — succeeded on the same tree.
**No deploy was attempted**; `mythuso.co.za` serves an earlier build,
and per the standing rule a deploy is the founder's to approve as its own step.

**Open.** The floor of 5 is proposed by "Safety lead (Wave 6)" and decided by nobody — `decidedBy` is null on its
default and both bounds, so Operations has to set it. At 5, four of the roster's six suburbs are below it and draw
counts with no proportion, which is what the roster honestly supports; at the highest bound of 20 no suburb draws
one anywhere, which the contract says should be somebody saying that out loud rather than drift. The overlay is
web only: the phones carry no dispatch map surface for it, and `emit-field-safety.mjs` emits nothing for it
because neither phone draws it. `rosteredIn()` counts the roster as it stands, so a suburb's denominator does not
follow who is actually on shift — a nurse covering a suburb she is not rostered to appears in the count and not in
the denominator, which is the honest direction of error and is asserted, but it means the proportion is about the
roster and not about this afternoon.

## Delivered — the patient's devices, live and simulated, on Triage and beside the consultation, 1 October 2026 (web, iOS and Android)

The founder's ask of 1 October 2026: "get that screen to work with live triage simulation all IoT devices — I
liked that screen — even on consultation the doctor sees them." The screen is the Lovable export's live triage
page. Built in its arrangement and without its claims: every instrument in the kit and the patient's own watch
streaming simulated readings, each with its unit, the instrument it stands for, its provenance, how long ago it
arrived, a trend line and where it stands against the record's range in words — and, where the export drew a
device triage, an early-warning score, an AI interpretation, an alarm centre and a risk heatmap, the contract's
sentence saying why none is drawn.

| What landed | What it refuses, and what did not move | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **The contract** `live-vitals.json`: seven streams (systolic, diastolic, pulse and oxygen from the oximeter, temperature, glucose, and the patient's own watch), each a `records.json#observations` measure on a `capture.json` instrument; the pace (a reading every 2 s, three readings per preset step, twelve kept for the trend); Park and Miller's jitter constants; the board's words; five refusals. Two presets in `devices/simulator-presets.json` gained glucose (`sim.well` a baseline, `sim.glucose` a rise) because no preset sent one | No range, unit, label or instrument name is typed: the label, unit, range and step are the record's and the instrument's name capture.json's; on the phones a stream names its measure and reads the range from `Records.observations` / `observationRanges`, never from the emitted copy. The scale and the ECG are listed as not streamed (the record holds no `weight` or `ecg` measure) and respiratory rate as counted by the nurse (no instrument measures it) — both worked out, not typed | `packages/catalog/live-vitals.json`, `scripts/emit-live-vitals.mjs` → `LiveVitalsData.swift`, `LiveVitalsData.kt` |
| **The arithmetic** `packages/engines/src/devices/live-vitals.ts`: a reading is a pure function of scenario, patient, stream and reading number — the preset's baseline at that step plus a jitter on the record's step — so the web, iOS (`Models/LiveVitals.swift`) and Android (`model/LiveVitals.kt`) show the same numbers; Swift and the web were compiled and compared over three scenarios and agree to the digit; Kotlin is the same integer arithmetic and was compiled but not run | No clock, no `Math.random`, nothing stored. It says inside, below or above the record's indicative range and nothing else: no score, priority, band or colour. Every reading carries `source: "simulator"`, `quality: "synthetic"`; the stale preset sends nothing live and says so in Devices' own stale sentence | engines, iOS, Android |
| **The screens.** Web: the doctor's Triage page draws `LiveVitalsBoard` under the sandbox's patient chips (it replaces the freshness tiles); the call room draws the compact `LiveVitalsPanel` in the patient summary beside the call; the consultation record's rail draws it for the doctor's record and the teleconsultation's write-up. Scenario select, Pause and Resume. iOS and Android: the compact panel in the call stage and at the top of the consultation record when the writer is a doctor | The simulated banner (`board.banner`) and the devices capability's notice over every board; the record's "not a validated early-warning score" caveat under it. No badge but the neutral one; the one warning colour is the banner. Nothing animates and only the running/paused sentence is a live region. The interval is cleared on unmount; no storage. Every piece behind a dynamic import — none of it on the patient's entry | `features/LiveVitals.tsx`, `live-vitals.css`, `DoctorPages.tsx`, `CallSummary.tsx`, `Consultation.tsx`, `Teleconsult.tsx`; `Features/LiveVitalsView.swift`; `ui/LiveVitalsScreens.kt` |
| **Checks** in `scripts/check-live-vitals.mjs`, called from `check-boundaries.mjs`, each proven to fire by `node scripts/prove-live-vitals.mjs` (20 breaks): the join, the refusals standing only while `clinical.json` names no triage protocol, no score/priority/severity word or coloured badge, no typed range, the banner and notice, no clock or random source, no storage, the interval cleared, nothing animated, no static import, both phones rendering the banner, notice and refusals and colouring nothing as danger. Engine tests `live-vitals.test.ts`; journey `tests/live-vitals.spec.ts` on both viewports | `tests/doctor-pages.spec.ts`'s Triage journey counted the freshness tiles; it now counts the board's streams and holds the score, heatmap and early-warning words to the refusals alone | `scripts/`, `tests/` |

The patient's entry, measured the CLAUDE.md way (every script, module preload and stylesheet
`apps/web/dist/index.html` references, gzip -9): **257.53 kB** across 15 files, measured on a working tree carrying other changes in
flight beside this one; none of the board's code, words or styles is in any of those files (its `LiveVitals` chunk
and stylesheet load only when a doctor opens Triage, a call or a consultation record), so the 0.26 kB over the
last recorded 257.27 kB is not this change's.

**Open — what a reading means.** Inside, below or above the record's indicative range is all the board says. A
score, a priority, an alarm or a ranking waits on a ratified triage protocol (`clinical.json#triage.triageProtocols`)
and, before any of them reads a real reading, on a device that carries clinical weight — the build stops when a
triage protocol is named, so the refusal sentences cannot outlive their truth.

## Delivered — Show GilbertOne a rash: a photo held on the phone, set questions and three outcomes the rules decide, 1 October 2026 (web, iOS and Android)

The founder's ask of 1 October 2026: take a picture of a skin rash, give information about what it might be,
and say whether a sister should see it or how to look after it. Built as intake plus general information,
because GilbertOne does symptom intake and not triage, and because nothing in this build may read a photo of
somebody's skin. **No model looks at the photo on any platform**, and the screen says so in the contract's words.

| What landed | What it refuses, and what did not move | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **The contract** `skin-check.json`: the photo's sentences (held on the phone, nothing reads it, video not taken), nine questions — who, where, since when, how it feels, what it looks like (nine descriptor chips), spreading, fever, five signs and "None of these", and anything new in her own words — and seven rules: two emergency (a rash that does not fade under a glass; swelling of the lips, face or tongue or trouble breathing), five for today (a large burn; blistering or peeling with a fever; a red, hot area spreading quickly with a fever; a rash spreading quickly with a fever; a baby younger than three months, kept with `keptBecause` for the reviewer). Every outcome sentence; the notes for the sister; `review.reviewedBy: null`; sixteen fixtures, two of them web-only | **An emergency rule is not a new emergency word**: it names one option whose own label the existing terms in `gilbert-emergency-terms.json` raise, the build refuses one they do not, and refuses any other option or question they raise. A rule for today reads the knowledge base's own guidance back and sets no priority. General information is "rashes like this are often…", never fewer than two entries when anything was described, always with "only a nurse or doctor who sees it can say what yours is". No digit and no you-have sentence addressed to the patient. Care steps come from the first-aid file only, never a condition's home care | `packages/catalog/skin-check.json` |
| **The photo reader, declared and refused everywhere**: `photoReading` waits on a ratified photo-reading protocol with a named clinical reviewer, an impact assessment that covers images, an Information Officer and a processor and residency decision — none exists. `route: null`, with the reason | **No route is declared in `apis/assistant.json`** and the build refuses one whose path names a photo, an image, vision or skin: the check sends no photo anywhere, and a production address with nothing behind it but a refusal is proposed only when the four things exist. Nothing in `apps/assistant-api` reads a photo | `packages/catalog/skin-check.json`, `scripts/check-skin-check.mjs` |
| **Knowledge**: seven conditions (contact dermatitis, hives, cellulitis, sunburn, heat rash, insect bites, a severe skin reaction to a medicine) and four first-aid entries (minor bites and stings, sunburn, the glass test for a rash, caring for an itchy rash at home), each with a source naming the page it was written from, `codes: {}` and a `review` block — `reviewedBy: null`, `awaiting-clinical-review`. The catalogue is 261 entries; the three tests that pin the count, `knowledge-corpus-tiers.json` and the two assistant tools that printed a typed count now read it | **Every added entry says nobody has reviewed it**, and the build refuses one that names a reviewer or one the check never shows. The emergency terms are unchanged. The entries also enter the corpus the live assistant's `knowledge_search` reads, on the next deploy | `packages/catalog/knowledge/conditions.json`, `first-aid.json`, `knowledge-corpus-tiers.json`, `apps/assistant-api/src/lib/tools/` |
| **The arithmetic** `packages/gilbertone/src/skin-check.ts`: typed words to the emergency terms and then the escalation ruleset (so "a rash and my lips are swelling" is an emergency), the emergency rules, the two required questions, the rules for today, general information last; `pressSkinOption`, the notes and the review sentences. Ported by hand to `Models/SkinCheck.swift` and `model/SkinCheck.kt`, generated data in `SkinCheckData.swift` / `.kt` by `scripts/emit-skin-check.mjs` (`npm run skin-check`), fixtures run by `skin-check.test.ts` and `SkinCheckFixturesTest.kt` | No network, no model, no storage. Since 2 October 2026 the phones carry the escalation ruleset too (`scripts/emit-escalation.mjs`), so the two fixtures it decides, web-only until then, run on all three platforms | `packages/gilbertone/src/skin-check.ts`, `apps/ios/MyThuso/Models/`, `apps/android/.../model/`, `scripts/emit-skin-check.mjs` |
| **The screens.** Web: "Show GilbertOne a rash" on the patient's GilbertOne opens `SkinCheck.tsx` in place of the conversation, on its own dynamic import inside the panel's. iOS: a sheet from GilbertOne's suggestions, PhotosPicker. Android: a full-screen dialog, the image-only photo picker and the camera's in-memory preview. On all three an emergency hands the words to the conversation's own emergency turn and the check closes | **The photo is never stored or sent**: one object URL, revoked by its own clean-up, no capture attribute, no `fetch`, storage or `FileReader` on the web; no save to the library, no file and no camera usage description on iOS; no file, no `FileProvider` and no camera permission on Android. **No video** — a video carries sound. Sending the notes is the handover submit route's `clinician-routing-not-built` refusal, read from the API contract | `apps/web/src/features/SkinCheck.tsx`, `skin-check.css`, `lib/skin-check.ts`, `Assistant.tsx`, `apps/ios/.../SkinCheckView.swift`, `AssistantView.swift`, `apps/android/.../SkinCheckScreens.kt`, `GilbertScreens.kt` |
| **Checks** in `scripts/check-skin-check.mjs`, called from `check-boundaries.mjs`; each proven to fire by `node scripts/prove-skin-check.mjs`. **Journey** `tests/skin-check.spec.ts` on both viewports: the photo shown from a blob URL, no request but a GET while it is held, nothing in either storage, the URL revoked when the check ends; a ticked sign and a typed sentence each reaching the emergency answer; a burn for today; the two required questions | Every rule above is a refusal the build makes, not a sentence it trusts | `scripts/check-skin-check.mjs`, `scripts/prove-skin-check.mjs`, `tests/skin-check.spec.ts` |

**Open — the sources' licences.** The new entries are written in MyThuso's own words, mostly from the NHS
website's pages, and each source names the public-domain federal pages (MedlinePlus health topics, CDC, NIOSH)
it was checked against. The same day's sources assessment (`docs/governance/KNOWLEDGE-SOURCES.md`) finds the NHS
website's content outside licence scope for a South African service and WHO's non-commercial only, so the WHO
and MedlinePlus-encyclopedia citations were dropped. Several details rest on the NHS pages alone — the glass test
is described on no public-domain page — and whether facts restated in our own words may stand on them, or must be
re-based on permitted sources, is the clinical reviewer's and the Information Officer's to decide before a real
patient reads them. The review pack's F6 asks it.

**Open — a rash on a young baby.** The rule stands on the founder's brief alone; no entry says it in those words.

| **The contract** `live-vitals.json`: seven streams (systolic, diastolic, pulse and oxygen from the oximeter, temperature, glucose, and the patient's own watch), each a `records.json#observations` measure on a `capture.json` instrument; the pace (a reading every 2 s, three readings per preset step, twelve kept for the trend); Park and Miller's jitter constants; the board's words; five refusals. Two presets in `devices/simulator-presets.json` gained glucose (`sim.well` a baseline, `sim.glucose` a rise) because no preset sent one | No range, unit, label or instrument name is typed: the label, unit, range and step are the record's and the instrument's name capture.json's; on the phones a stream names its measure and reads the range from `Records.observations` / `observationRanges`, never from the emitted copy. The scale and the ECG are listed as not streamed (the record holds no `weight` or `ecg` measure) and respiratory rate as counted by the nurse (no instrument measures it) — both worked out, not typed | `packages/catalog/live-vitals.json`, `scripts/emit-live-vitals.mjs` → `LiveVitalsData.swift`, `LiveVitalsData.kt` |
| **The arithmetic** `packages/engines/src/devices/live-vitals.ts`: a reading is a pure function of scenario, patient, stream and reading number — the preset's baseline at that step plus a jitter on the record's step — so the web, iOS (`Models/LiveVitals.swift`) and Android (`model/LiveVitals.kt`) show the same numbers; Swift and the web were compiled and compared over three scenarios and agree to the digit; Kotlin is the same integer arithmetic and was compiled but not run | No clock, no `Math.random`, nothing stored. It says inside, below or above the record's indicative range and nothing else: no score, priority, band or colour. Every reading carries `source: "simulator"`, `quality: "synthetic"`; the stale preset sends nothing live and says so in Devices' own stale sentence | engines, iOS, Android |

Scenario select, Pause and Resume. iOS and Android: the compact panel in the call stage and at the top of the consultation record when the writer is a doctor | The simulated banner (`board.banner`) and the devices capability's notice over every board; the record's "not a validated early-warning score" caveat under it. No badge but the neutral one; the one warning colour is the banner. Nothing animates and only the running/paused sentence is a live region. The interval is cleared on unmount; no storage. Every piece behind a dynamic import — none of it on the patient's entry | `features/LiveVitals.tsx`, `live-vitals.css`, `DoctorPages.tsx`, `CallSummary.tsx`, `Consultation.tsx`, `Teleconsult.tsx`; `Features/LiveVitalsView.swift`; `ui/LiveVitalsScreens.kt` |

Engine tests `live-vitals.test.ts`; journey `tests/live-vitals.spec.ts` on both viewports | `tests/doctor-pages.spec.ts`'s Triage journey counted the freshness tiles; it now counts the board's streams and holds the score, heatmap and early-warning words to the refusals alone | `scripts/`, `tests/` |

The patient's entry, measured the CLAUDE.md way (every script, module preload and stylesheet
`apps/web/dist/index.html` references, gzip -9): **257.53 kB** across 15 files, measured on a working tree carrying other changes in
flight beside this one; none of the board's code, words or styles is in any of those files (its `LiveVitals` chunk
and stylesheet load only when a doctor opens Triage, a call or a consultation record), so the 0.26 kB over the
last recorded 257.27 kB is not this change's.

**Open — what a reading means.** Inside, below or above the record's indicative range is all the board says. A
score, a priority, an alarm or a ranking waits on a ratified triage protocol (`clinical.json#triage.triageProtocols`)
and, before any of them reads a real reading, on a device that carries clinical weight — the build stops when a
triage protocol is named, so the refusal sentences cannot outlive their truth.
